notes: Summary: Enterprise e-comm platform evaluating Redwood for chat + reranking + embeddings in checkout and search. Primary technical blocker: ability to handle extreme short-duration QPS bursts during flash sales and promotions without queueing or p95 tail regressions. Internal requirement: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for checkout-affecting calls; sustained throughput ~600 QPS, burst capacity spikes to 10k-15k QPS for 30-120s windows. POC outcomes: hosted API straightforward for baseline, but in replay tests we saw queuing and token generation p95 spikes (~1.1s) at ~8k concurrent when autoscaling/instance types were default. Recommended path from SE: Dedicated reserved pools + aggressive autoscaling + prefix/KV caching + routing rules to funnel non-critical workloads to cheaper models. Ventaris concerns: unpredictability of cost during bursts, potential for queue build-up impacting checkout flow, and preference from infra team for on-prem or guaranteed-reserved capacity. Sales notes: procurement froze budget after competitor offered a pre-reserved on-premish solution at lower headline cost; also no strong internal champion after CTO moved to new role. Quotes: CTO (both calls) - "We cannot accept >200ms p95 for checkout; even short tail spikes cost us conversions." Action history: multiple technical callbacks, two perf replays, one security questionnaire answered. Current status: stalled/closed-to-competitor for now. Next recommended steps: capture exact burst SLAs, produce a Tail Latency Mitigation plan (detailed cost estimate for Dedicated + burst pool), and re-open after Ventaris FY/Q cycle (target Q2).
